config.no_folder: No folder for config.toml was found
feature.analyse.a1: Yes. Analyse works on any Game, whether you played it or opened it from a database.
feature.analyse.a2: Not while a rated game against a person is live online. It comes back when the game ends.
feature.analyse.q1: Can I analyse a game I did not play in Bragd?
feature.analyse.title: Analyse
feature.analyse.what: Step through a Game, try other moves, and let an Engine evaluate each position.
feature.databases.a1: No. Bragd reads a Foreign database in place, and only rewrites it when you choose Save.
feature.databases.a2: Two Games with the same moves from the same start are one Game in a Library, whatever their headers say. It remembers every Source it came from.
feature.databases.q1: Does opening a PGN file change it?
feature.databases.title: Databases
feature.databases.what: Open game files in their own formats, or import them into a Library where each Game appears once.
feature.disk.a1: Only when you turn that on for a Source. Otherwise Disk watch only warns you.
feature.disk.a2: A filter on the Games a Source's Route keeps, such as a minimum rating or a time control. Each Route pairs one with a Library, and a Game no Route keeps is never stored.
feature.disk.q1: Does Bragd delete anything by itself?
feature.disk.title: Disk watch
feature.disk.what: Shows what Bragd keeps on disk, warns at the limits you set, and can strip downloads to the Games you want.
feature.engines.a1: Bragd uses an installed Engine first. Otherwise it can pull a sealed container image with podman or docker.
feature.engines.a2: Tafl, ur and senet have no outside Engine. They get Bragd's own built-in Bots.
feature.engines.q1: Do I have to install an Engine?
feature.engines.q2: Why is there no Engine for tafl?
feature.engines.title: Engines
feature.engines.what: Programs that play and evaluate positions, found on this machine or run from a sealed container image.
feature.families.a1: Settings → Game families, or the install wizard. Each Family and each Variant has its own switch.
feature.families.a2: Nothing is deleted. Its files still open, with a banner offering to turn it back on.
feature.families.q1: Where do I turn a game off?
feature.families.q2: What happens to my games of a Family I turn off?
feature.families.title: Game families
feature.families.what: Every Game family Bragd plays, each with its Variants. Turn off what you do not play.
feature.helper.a1: It fetches Sources, indexes your Libraries and finds Duplicates, so the windows stay quick.
feature.helper.a2: Ten minutes after the last window closes, unless Start with my session is on.
feature.helper.title: The Helper
feature.helper.what: A background process shared by every Bragd window that fetches, indexes and finds Duplicates.
feature.play.a1: Yes: play against an Engine, against yourself on one board, or online.
feature.play.a2: Each Variant names its own Sides: White and Black, Red and Black, Sente and Gote, Attackers and Defenders.
feature.play.q1: Can I play both Sides myself?
feature.play.q2: Why are the Sides not called White and Black?
feature.play.title: Play
feature.play.what: Start a Game of any Variant that is on, against an Engine, against yourself or online.
feature.tablebases.a1: 3–5 pieces, about 1 GB, covers most endgames. 6 pieces is a large download; 7 pieces is a folder you bring yourself.
feature.tablebases.a2: Only when the tables you have do not cover a position, and only while Ask Lichess for tablebase positions is on.
feature.tablebases.q2: When does a position go to Lichess?
feature.tablebases.title: Tablebases
feature.tablebases.what: Perfect play for chess positions with few pieces, from Syzygy tables, passed to every Engine.
feature.themes.a1: Racing green, Bragd's own, built on the colours of its icon.
feature.themes.a2: No. A Board theme never inverts with a dark Theme: the light squares stay the lighter ones.
feature.themes.q2: Does a dark Theme turn the board dark?
feature.themes.title: Themes
feature.themes.what: Thirty built-in Themes, a Look laid over them, your own Themes in config.toml, and four Board themes.
feature.update.a1: No. It only tells you. Updating is left to the way you installed it, so your package manager stays in charge.
feature.update.a2: Untick Check for a new version in Settings → Privacy and updates.
feature.update.q2: How do I turn the check off?
feature.update.title: Update checks
feature.update.what: At start and once a day, asks where Bragd was installed from whether a newer release exists, and names the command that upgrades your copy.
feature.wizard.a1: Yes: Settings → Overview → Run the install wizard again.
feature.wizard.a2: What's new in the sidebar lists every version with its cards.
feature.wizard.q1: Can I run the wizard again?
feature.wizard.q2: Where do I see what came in a version?
feature.wizard.title: Install wizard and What's new
feature.wizard.what: On the first start, six short steps set up Bragd. After an upgrade, cards show what is new.
feature.parquet.a1: No. The export only reads the Library, and the file is a copy.
feature.parquet.a2: DuckDB, and any other tool that reads Parquet. Bragd itself never reads the file back.
feature.parquet.q1: Does the export change the Library?
feature.parquet.title: Export to Parquet
feature.parquet.what: Write a Library to a Parquet file, to query its Games with DuckDB.

setting.theme.hint: The app's colours, and with some Themes their own shapes. Racing green is the default.

feature.tips.title: Tips
feature.tips.what: Now and then, one line suggests a feature you have not used yet, with Show me, Not now and Don't suggest this again.
feature.tips.q1: How do I see fewer Tips, or none?
feature.tips.a1: Settings → Tips: Often, Now and then (the default) or Off. Don't suggest this again silences one Tip for good.
feature.tips.q2: Does Bragd send what I use anywhere?
feature.tips.a2: No. The counts stay in Bragd's state file on this machine.
feature.tips.a3: At start or when Bragd has been idle a while, never during a live Game or the wizard, and never for a feature you already use.
tour.tips.title: Tips
tour.tips.text: Now and then Bragd suggests a feature you have not tried. Set how often in Settings → Tips.

feature.families.tip: Play only some of the games? Turn the others off in Settings → Game families, and Bragd shows only yours.
feature.tips.tip: Tips come once a week. Settings → Tips makes them daily, or turns them off.

feature.helper.tip: The Helper can fetch Sources on a schedule: turn one on in Settings → Knowledge.

feature.analyse.tip: Analyse lets an Engine evaluate every position of a Game.
feature.tablebases.tip: Syzygy tablebases give perfect play with few pieces left: Tablebases in the sidebar.

feature.clubs.title: Clubs
feature.clubs.what: Members with roles and IDs in one Club file, Glicko-2 or Elo club ratings with an audit log, and players found in the rating lists of FIDE and national federations.
feature.clubs.q1: How do I share a Club?
feature.clubs.a1: Copy its .bragd-club file, or keep it in a shared folder. A lock stops two directors changing it at once.
feature.clubs.a2: A director. Every change goes into the audit log with who, when, the old and new values and why.
feature.clubs.q3: Where do the rating lists come from?
feature.clubs.a3: From FIDE and the national federations listed under chess's Sources (the DSU, the ECF, the CFC, the SShL and the NZCF), fetched once a month by the Helper once you turn them on. Nothing is downloaded before that.
feature.clubs.tip: Keep your club's members and ratings in Bragd: Clubs in the sidebar.
tour.clubs.title: Clubs
tour.clubs.text: Clubs in the sidebar keeps a club's members, roles, FIDE, national and Lichess IDs, and Glicko-2 or Elo ratings with an audit log, all in one file you can share. Rating lists from FIDE and national federations help you find players by name or ID.
matches.intro: Let Engines play each other in the Helper: a round robin, a gauntlet, or two Engines until the SPRT decides. Every Game goes into a Library.
matches.engines_hint: In a gauntlet or an SPRT, the first Engine ticked is the one tested.
matches.none: No Engine is there to run for this Variant yet.
matches.kind.sprt_with: SPRT: H0 {elo0} Elo, H1 {elo1} Elo, α {alpha}, β {beta}
matches.rounds_sprt: At most this many game pairs
matches.period: Moves per period (0: the whole Game)
matches.tablebases: End chess endgames by the tablebases
matches.title: {variant}: {engines}
matches.sprt: LLR {llr} (bounds {lower} and {upper}): {verdict}. Elo from game pairs: {elo}
matches.sprt_two: An SPRT is between exactly two Engines.
matches.sprt_bounds: H1 must be above H0, and α and β between 0 and 0.5.
feature.matches.title: Engine matches
feature.matches.what: Engines play each other in the Helper: a round robin, a gauntlet, or a two-Engine match the SPRT stops, with books, adjudication and Games at once.
feature.matches.a1: Whether the first Engine is stronger by the H1 Elo difference or only by H0. It stops the match as soon as the Games are enough, with the error chances α and β.
feature.matches.a2: Into the Library you choose, matches.bragd by default, as they end. Open it under Databases.
feature.matches.q3: Can I close Bragd while a match runs?
feature.matches.a3: Yes. The match runs in the Helper. If the Helper stops, the match goes on where it was when the Helper starts again.
feature.matches.tip: Find out which Engine is stronger: Engine matches in the sidebar.
tour.matches.title: Engine matches
tour.matches.text: Engine matches in the sidebar lets Engines play each other in the Helper: a round robin, a gauntlet, or two Engines until the SPRT decides. Openings come from a book, lost or drawn Games are adjudicated, and every Game goes into a Library.
matches.draw: Call a level Game a draw
tournaments.error.no_legal_pairing: No pairing of this Round meets the absolute rules. Pair it by hand.
tournaments.error.too_complex: This Round mixes too many scores to pair on its own. Pair it by hand.

tournaments.error.name: A Tournament needs a name of up to 100 characters.
tournaments.error.rounds: A Swiss Tournament has from 1 to 99 Rounds.

feature.leagues.title: Team Leagues
feature.leagues.what: Run a Club's team League: Teams meet in a round-robin on a set number of boards, with line-ups, board results, and standings by match points, then board points.
feature.leagues.q1: Who has White on which board?
feature.leagues.a1: The home Team has White on boards 1, 3, 5 and so on, and the away Team on the others.
feature.leagues.q2: What if a Team is a player short?
feature.leagues.a2: Leave that board empty in its line-up. The board can then only be a forfeit, won by the player who is there.
feature.leagues.q3: How are the standings worked out?
feature.leagues.a3: A match won gives 2 match points and a draw 1. Teams level on match points are ordered by board points.
feature.leagues.tip: Run your club's team league in Bragd: Clubs in the sidebar, then New League.
tour.leagues.title: Team Leagues
tour.leagues.text: A Club now runs team Leagues: add the Teams in board order, pair each Round by the Berger tables, set the line-ups, enter the board results, and follow the standings by match points and board points.
leagues.error.name: A League needs a name of up to 100 characters.
leagues.error.boards: A League plays on 1 to 20 boards a match.
leagues.error.started: A League takes no new Teams once Round 1 is paired.
leagues.error.team_name: A Team needs a name of up to 100 characters, not one another Team has.
leagues.error.too_few: A League needs at least two Teams.
leagues.error.line_up: A line-up names one player a board, from the Team, in board order.
leagues.error.forfeit: A board with a player missing can only be a forfeit.
leagues.error.missing: This League is no longer in the Club file.

tournaments.system.dutch.hint: FIDE's Swiss: players on the same points meet, the top half of each score group against the bottom half.
tournaments.system.monrad.hint: Numbers are drawn by lot. Each Round, from the top of the standings, each player meets the nearest one below not yet met.
tournaments.system.nordic.hint: The Danish Chess Union's Swiss: players are numbered by strength, and in each score group the strong half meets the weak half.
tournaments.system.drop_in.hint: Whoever comes on the evening is paired. An absence counts half a point for the pairing only, and the standings run over the season.
tournaments.system.round_robin.hint: Everyone meets everyone once, by FIDE's Berger tables.
tournaments.system.double_round_robin.hi: Everyone meets everyone twice, once with each colour.
tournaments.system.knockout.hint: The loser of each match is out. When the field is not a power of two, the top seeds go straight to Round 2.
tournaments.system.scheveningen.hint: Team 1 against team 2: every player meets every player of the other team once.
tournaments.system.double_scheveningen.h: Team 1 against team 2, twice: every player meets every player of the other team once with each colour.
tournaments.baku: Baku acceleration: the top half gets extra points for pairing the first Rounds
tournaments.warn.not_bracket: This is not the knockout bracket's pairing for this Round.
tournaments.warn.not_schedule: This is not the Scheveningen schedule's pairing for this Round.
tournaments.error.teams: A Scheveningen needs two teams of the same size: put each player in team 1 or team 2.
tournaments.error.playoff: Enter the play-off winner of every drawn knockout match before pairing the next Round.
tournaments.error.playoff_player: A play-off winner is one of the two players of a knockout match.
tournaments.error.knockout_settled: The next knockout Round was paired from this match, so its winner stands.
tournaments.error.drop_in_half_bye: A Drop-in has no half-point byes: a player who is away counts half a point for the pairing anyway.
tournaments.title: Tournaments
tournaments.name: Name
tournaments.handicap: Handicap games: the weaker player takes Black, one stone for each 100 rating points
tournaments.new_hint: A round-robin, knockout or Scheveningen works out its Rounds from its players when Round 1 is paired. The tiebreaks start as the Danish Chess Union's, and you can change them.
tournaments.remove_confirm: Delete the Tournament {name} with all its Rounds and results? An exported bundle keeps a copy.
tournaments.players_hint: Register players before the night or as they come. Only players who are checked in are paired.
tournaments.show_hint: The pairings open in a window of their own in large type. Drag it to a projector or a second screen, or print it from there.
tournaments.why_pair_again: Why pair this Round again? A late arrival, say. The log keeps the reason.
tournaments.why_correction: Why correct this result? The log keeps the reason.
tournaments.check_first: Check the pairing first: Bragd says what rules it breaks.
tournaments.tiebreaks_hint: Players level on points are ordered by the first tiebreak, then the next, as FIDE's rules C.07 say.
tournaments.rate_hint: Work out the members' club ratings from the games they played each other here. It can be done once, when every result is in.
tournaments.rated: The Club's ratings count this Tournament's games.
tournaments.exports_hint: To publish, save the standings page and put it on the club's website or a notice board.
tournaments.export.html.hint: One page with the standings, the crosstable and every Round, to publish.
tournaments.export.trf.hint: FIDE's Tournament Report File, for rating reports and other pairing programs.
tournaments.export.pgn.hint: Every game played, with the players, the Round and the result.
tournaments.export.bundle.hint: The whole Tournament with its log, to open in another Club or keep as a copy.
tournaments.dsu: The Danish Chess Union publishes no file format for rating reports: results are typed into its web system, which takes the games as PGN.
feature.tournaments.title: Tournaments
feature.tournaments.what: Run a Club's Tournament on the night, Swiss, Monrad, Nordic Swiss, Drop-in, round-robin, knockout or Scheveningen: check in, pair, show the pairings on a second screen, enter results, and publish standings with FIDE's tiebreaks.
feature.tournaments.q1: Can I change a pairing Bragd made?
feature.tournaments.a1: Yes, as a director, before any result is in. Bragd says which rules the change breaks, and the log keeps it with your reason.
feature.tournaments.a2: FIDE's set from C.07, such as Buchholz, Sonneborn-Berger and direct encounter, in the order you choose. A new Tournament starts with the Danish Chess Union's.
feature.tournaments.q3: How do I send results for rating?
feature.tournaments.a3: Save the FIDE report (TRF) for FIDE, or the games as PGN for the Danish Chess Union's web system.
feature.tournaments.tip: Run your club's tournament in Bragd: Clubs in the sidebar, then New Tournament.
tour.tournaments.title: Tournaments
tour.tournaments.text: A Club now runs its own Tournaments: Swiss (FIDE Dutch, with Baku acceleration if you like), Monrad, Nordic Swiss, Drop-in, round-robin, knockout and Scheveningen. Register and check in players, pair each Round, show the pairings on a second screen, enter and correct results, and publish standings and a crosstable. Exports: FIDE TRF, PGN and a bundle.
common.offline: Bragd is offline, so nothing is downloaded.

player.open: {name}: results, rating and openings in this Library
player.find_hint: Start of a name, such as Carlsen
feature.players.title: Player summary
feature.players.what: One player's Games in a Library at a glance: results by side, score, rating over time, openings, best wins and worst losses.
feature.players.q1: How do I open a player's summary?
feature.players.a1: Click their name in a Library's Games list, or type the start of it in Find a player on the Libraries tab.
feature.players.q2: Why are there no openings or ratings?
feature.players.a2: Openings come from ECO codes, which only chess Games have. A rating shows only where the Games' headers give one.
feature.players.q3: Does it cover all my Libraries?
feature.players.a3: No. A summary covers the Library it was opened from, in the Families you play.
feature.players.tip: Click a player's name in a Library's Games list to see their results, rating and openings.
tour.players.title: Player summary
tour.players.text: Click a name in a Library's Games list, or use Find a player, to see that player's results, rating over time, openings and best wins.
positions.title: Position store
positions.hint: Engine Evaluations and Annotations, kept by position for every Game. Export writes them to a Parquet file. Import merges such a file in and keeps the deeper result for each position.
feature.positions.title: Position store
feature.positions.what: Engine Evaluations and Annotations are kept by position, so a position judged once shows at once in every Game.
feature.positions.q1: Does deleting a Library lose its analysis?
feature.positions.a1: No. The Position store is apart from the Libraries.
feature.positions.q2: How do I move it to another machine?
feature.positions.a2: Settings → Knowledge → Disk watch → Export Position store, then Import Position store on the other machine.
feature.positions.tip: Back up your Engine analysis: Export Position store in Disk watch.
feature.annotations.title: Annotations
feature.annotations.what: A review marks each move ?? ? ?! ! or !!, names the better move and, in chess, a fork, a pin, a hanging piece or a missed mate.
feature.annotations.a1: By how much the move lost by the Engine's score: in pawns, in the chance to win for go, or in equity for backgammon.
feature.annotations.q2: Why does a second review finish at once?
feature.annotations.a2: Each position the Engine judged is kept in the Position store, and is not judged again.
feature.annotations.tip: Review the game in Analyse to see which moves lost ground and what was better.
tour.positions.title: Analysis is kept by position
tour.positions.text: A position an Engine has judged shows at once in Analyse and in every review of a Game that reaches it. Export and import it in Disk watch.
tour.annotations.title: Annotations
tour.annotations.text: Review the game marks each move, names the better line and, in chess, a fork, a pin, a hanging piece or a missed mate.
